paragraphs: VODA.ai sells decision support software to water utilities. The point is helping engineers decide which pipes to replace, assess, monitor or investigate next.

Projects start from data a utility already keeps, such as GIS records, pipe attributes, historical break records, work orders and service line information. Machine learning then flags pipes with an elevated likelihood of failure, including ones that have never broken. Utilities do not need clean records to begin. Initial model outputs, risk scores and prioritized watch lists are often available within three to six months. The same approach supports lead service line programs, sorting likely galvanized lines and prioritizing field verification before replacement work.

The company is Boston-based and was founded in 2017. It says it has worked in 31 states and eight countries and analyzed more than a million miles of pipe. Executives from 78 water utilities at the Smart Water Summit picked it as best smart water solution. Published case studies include lead compliance work in Rock Hill, South Carolina.
